set.st: July 1939: the three young Belote boys dug up a drain tile holding $1,880 in $5/$10/$20 gold (1882-1902) on the farm 4-4½ mi NW-W of Bronson, on the Matteson-Bronson township line; days later Frank Belote kicked up an iron pipe with $1,120 in gold 12 ft away. A second tile, plugged with concrete at both ends, which the boys had used as a toy smokestack, was never found again. Owner Kregger ordered no more digging and evicted the Belotes. The original owner, who died 17 Apr 1909, was said to have buried several lots of gold; a buried safe was dug up on the farm soon after his death, c.1909, and the owner had plowed up a pipe of gold the year before the tile find. Pin is on the farmsteads at the township line, not the spot itself. In Jan 1941 Judge Renshaw split the $3,000 found in 1939 half to the finders and half to the heirs of the former owners. The AP account puts the $1,100 in a tin can under the front porch and adds a third cache of $100. The local papers add: it was the old Canaris 'Canary' Phillips farm (Canarius Napoleon Phillips, 22 Aug 1829 - 17 Apr 1909, buried in Matteson; his widow Alzina died 4 Feb 1921, the source of the papers' '1921'), bought by Kregger from a Chicago man. The tile lay barely under the surface in an open field near a clothes-line standard; a pipe plowed up the year before had been tossed in a fence corner; a small safe of money was unearthed soon after Phillips's death, c.1909. The Free Press said Phillips 'banked most of his solid cash in secret places of burial about his farm'. The gold was legally the Phillips estate's, hence the 1941 split.
pinev: 1915 Branch atlas Matteson plate: C. N. Phillips 40, easternmost N-S strip of S½ sec 32 T6S R8W on the township line; the Bronson plate shows the estate strip continuing across N sec 5. 1900 census puts the widow in Matteson Twp.

On 2017 Michigan 1 m lidar two farmyard pads sit on the township-line road: one N of the road at about 41.8981,-85.2563 (sec 32, just W of the strip) and one S of it at about 41.8971,-85.2551 (N end of the sec 5 strip). No 1938 aerial read; the ring covers both yards.

1915 Bronson Twp plate: C. N. Phillips 86.56 ac in N sec 5 T7S R8W directly S of the Matteson 40, so the ~127-acre farm straddles the township line; the S yard at the N end of sec 5 is the likelier house. Phillips's only land E of town (20 ac in sec 11, Bronson Twp) was sold in 1897, so the '2 mi E' is an error.

pinev: Five Mile Hill crest, named in the 1900 Tribune; Baty's 90-ft shaft was sunk from the crest. Crest is the highest point of the dune mass south of the harbour on 2016 Michigan 1 m lidar (237.7 m).
'Just back of the summit' (Grand Rapids Herald 1900), i.e. the landward (east) side of the crest, within the 250 m ring.

Five Mile Hill named as the dune on the state park's east boundary (WPA 1941); name still in use 1934. On lidar the mass has two knobs: 226 m at 43.0561,-86.2413 right above the park and the 237.7 m summit 320 m east, joined by a saddle near 205 m; the 400 m ring covers both.

The Grand Haven city water storage tanks stood on Five Mile Hill (Muskegon Chronicle 1932). On 2016 lidar a round levelled pad about 32 m across sits on the summit at 232 m (43.0564,-86.2371) with a second small pad just S and an access road winding up: the tank site. Pin moved onto it (about 55 m from the old crest pin); the 400 m ring is kept so the W knob stays inside.
The tank pad is in the NW¼ of sec 29 T8N R16W (BLM PLSS), where the 1912 Ottawa plat shows a 'City of Grand Haven' strip just S of the channel: city water-works ground.

src: Plat book of Ottawa County (1912), Grand Haven Twp
